items.headline: Mastercard launches AI tool to surface forgotten card perks
items.summary: Mastercard announced Mastercard Max, an AI tool combining Mastercard and bank-supplied benefits to help cardholders navigate forgotten perks. The launch signals growing deployment of consumer-facing AI in financial services.

items.headline: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $44 billion
items.summary: CrowdStrike announced a $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler, positioning itself to capture rising demand for AI security amid vendor consolidation. Analysts see it closing a significant competitive gap with Palo Alto Networks.

items.headline: Jensen Huang ousted from Nvidia amid affair and spying scandal
items.summary: Jensen Huang is suddenly out as Nvidia's leader following revelations of an affair with a woman accused of funneling information to China. His departure has rattled investors already anxious about the AI sector.

items.headline: Asia AI stock rout forces Seoul and Taipei to intervene
items.summary: Governments in South Korea and Taiwan are trying to stabilize markets after a brutal selloff led by Samsung and TSMC. Both economies depend heavily on AI exports, leaving policymakers in a bind.

items.headline: Enterprises say AI regulation won't halt corporate innovation
items.summary: Technology leaders say the midterms settled that there will be no federal ceiling on AI regulation soon, leaving state laws as the operating standard. Companies plan to continue AI investment despite a patchwork of state-level rules.

items.headline: Big AI labs accused of learning enterprise customers' methods
items.summary: A Fortune analysis warns that AI labs seeing proprietary methods across thousands of enterprise customers can build those edges into defaults and sell them to competitors. The practice, while legal under current contracts, raises competitive and data-governance concerns.

items.headline: TechCrunch: how early backers bet big on Anthropic
items.summary: Notable Capital, GIC and Baillie Gifford made outsized bets on Anthropic before its record-breaking IPO, including Notable pouring roughly 10% of its fund into the Series E. The wagers paid off as Anthropic debuted at a multi-trillion-dollar valuation.

items.headline: OpenAI chief scientist proposes industry-wide AI limits
items.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist Jakub Pachocki suggested AI developers adopt common limits on powerful models and use 'perplexity' as a shared metric for measuring progress. The proposal comes amid heightened debate over pacing frontier AI development.

items.headline: Google Gemini 4 Carbon undercuts Anthropic on API pricing
items.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon publicly available, pricing it below Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 on the API. The move intensifies price competition among frontier model providers.

items.headline: China's AI ambitions hit a funding problem
items.summary: As Anthropic and other US labs raise tens of billions, Chinese AI startups are struggling to find capital to keep pace with soaring model-training costs. The gap underscores a widening financial divide in the US-China AI race.

items.headline: US chip curbs pummel China tech stocks, spur self-sufficiency
items.summary: A flurry of new US measures targeting China's access to advanced AI chips battered Chinese technology stocks this week. Investors are weighing whether Washington's curbs will meaningfully slow Beijing's AI progress.

items.headline: Anthropic's historic IPO raises over $81 billion
items.summary: Anthropic completed a record-breaking Nasdaq debut under ticker 'ANT', raising more than $81 billion at a valuation near $1.5 trillion. The listing makes it the only true public AI company in the US and a major test for the sector.

items.headline: House lawmakers form AI Safety and Innovation Caucus
items.summary: A bipartisan group of lawmakers launched the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus the same day Anthropic went public, focusing on AI regulation and safety. The move reflects rising congressional scrutiny of frontier AI risks.

items.headline: Anthropic's Wall Street debut puts AI's promise to the test
items.summary: Anthropic notched a valuation of about $2 trillion in its Nasdaq debut, edging past SpaceX's June listing. The debut capped a turbulent stretch for the AI sector and drew scrutiny over its path to profitability.

items.headline: IMF warns AI demand could push central banks to raise rates
items.summary: The head of the IMF warned at APEC that booming AI demand will force the world's most powerful central banks to raise interest rates. The warning highlights macroeconomic risks tied to the AI investment boom.

items.headline: Google introduces Gemini 4 Neon with frontier intelligence
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon on November 18, bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across software engineering, knowledge work, and science. It began rolling out to developers, enterprises, and consumers the same day.

items.headline: The Economist: self-improving AI models are coming
items.summary: A report by think-tank Metr estimated AI capabilities are growing roughly twice as fast as a year earlier, driven by AI-assisted development. Insiders expect 2027 to be the year systems become capable of building their own successors, raising recursive self-improvement concerns.

items.headline: Fortune: AI boom enters its 'final stages' as Anthropic IPOs
items.summary: Fortune reports the AI boom may be reaching its final stages as Anthropic goes public amid a jobless-growth economy delivering neither jobs nor growth. Goldman Sachs predicts a low-hire, low-fire labor market for another year before AI displacement grows.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic launched two new frontier models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, setting record-high benchmark scores alongside a 20% API cost reduction. It marks the company's first frontier release since CEO Dario Amodei called to slow the pace of AI development.
